Documentation → Administration → Settings

Settings (Admin Console)

Overview of the Settings page — called the Admin Console for administrators — with every group and tab, who can see it, and where each one is documented.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage profiles.manage advisor.configure
📍 WhereTop bar → Settings (URL /settings/)
On this page
  • What it is
  • How the menu works
  • Every group and tab
  • Permissions at a glance
  • Where settings are stored
  • Settings edited on other pages
  • Related

What it is#

Settings (/settings/) is one page with a grouped side menu. For administrators the page is titled Admin Console and opens on General; every other user sees a page titled Settings that contains only the My Account group and opens on Security.

  • Administrator here means a profile that grants users.manage (the seeded admin profile, Administrator). Ten of the eleven groups are shown only to administrators.
  • My Account (Security, Change Password) is shown to every signed-in user (Viewer and up).
  • The Scout entry (the AI assistant) additionally requires advisor.configure, and the Profiles entry profiles.manage; an administrator without the key does not see the entry.

A group with nothing you may see is not drawn at all, so the menu never offers a section that is not there.

How the menu works#

  • The menu is an accordion: all groups start collapsed, opening one group (or selecting a tab in it) folds the others, and the browser remembers the last group you opened.
  • Each tab has a fixed address (/settings/#tab-<name>), so a bookmark or a link such as /settings/#tab-auth opens that tab directly. After a save, the page returns to the tab the form was on.
  • An entry with the leaving arrow (↗) is a page, not a tab: Integrations replaces the console with its own page.
  • Sentinel → Settings also exists as a standalone page, /settings/sentinel, with the same menu beside it; on that page the menu entries link back into the console.

Permissions at a glance#

🔑Permission

  • Almost every save on this page checks users.manage (legacy key user_manage) and answers 403 Forbidden without it — even if the address is typed directly.
  • Scout (AI assistant) routes check advisor.configure.
  • Sentinel → Settings and Path Diagnostics → Settings are saved with users.manage, like every other administrator tab. The standalone /settings/sentinel page opens for any user with a view permission, but its save answers 403 Forbidden without users.manage (see Sentinel settings).
  • Security and Change Password act only on your own account and need no permission.
  • Independently of this page, the IP whitelist on Access Control applies to every non-administrator on every page.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Sentinel and Path Diagnostics (then called Scout) settings can only be saved with users.manage (before, any user with a change permission could save them by a direct request), and the Profiles tab is shown only with profiles.manage.

ℹ️Note

Changed on 2026-10-14: two labels were swapped. The AI assistant's tab under System, formerly AI Advisor, is now Scout; the group for the fault-localisation ladder, formerly Scout, is now Path Diagnostics. The tab addresses (#tab-ai, #tab-scout) did not change.

Where settings are stored#

Almost every value on this page is stored in the database table app_settings, which is replicated to the standby node of a high-availability pair, so a value set on the primary applies to both. Exceptions are machine-specific actions such as Services and Libraries on General, which act on the node you are connected to (with an explicit option to include the peer). Secrets (passwords, tokens, API keys) are stored encrypted and are never shown again; a blank secret field always means keep the stored value.

Settings edited on other pages#

Some values are not on this page even though they are configuration:

  • Your top-bar banner and your interface language are personal and set on your profile page (see Users and profiles).
  • Naming patterns, the classification vocabulary and network segments have their own pages (see Naming, Classification and Segments).
  • Collection targets and cadence for metrics are on the Metrics pages.
  • Scheduled actions (including the SoT harvest and the nightly system backup that Configuration SoT and Backup Server edit) are listed under Scheduled actions.

Related#

  • System backup — download and restore SATOM's own bundles.
  • Audit log — every save on this page writes an audit entry (settings.*).
  • Permissions — the full list of permission keys.
